text: You’re deep in flow, crafting something important on your computer. Your mind is buzzing, and the document is almost perfect.
Time to close it down, move to the next task. You hit 'Exit' or 'Close Window,' expecting instant dismissal.
But then, a pop-up: 'Save changes?' It's a small speed bump, a moment of friction. Why does it even ask? You know what you're doing!
This tiny delay is a guardian. It catches the moments you *don't* know what you're doing – like an accidental keypress. It’s pure loss aversion in action.
Imagine the alternative: no prompt. Just instant closure. One accidental click, and hours of work vanish into the digital void, leaving frustration and wasted time.
So, that little pop-up isn't an annoyance; it's a silent sentinel, always there to protect your effort. It ensures your digital world works *for* you, not against you.
